chunks: 2955 - And in the narration of al-Fuḍayl, he said:

I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام. I said: “I entered for ʿumrah, so where should I cut off the talbiyah?” He said: “At the point parallel to al-ʿAqabah, the ʿAqabah of the people of Madinah.” I said: “Where is the ʿAqabah of the people of Madinah?” He said: “At the point parallel to the dyers.”

key_terms.التَّلْبِيَةَ: the pilgrimage invocation recited in iḥrām
key_terms.الْعَقَبَةِ: the ascent or mountain pass used here as a landmark
key_terms.الْقَصَّارِينَ: the dyers; a known local area or marketplace landmark

ai.seo_question: Where does a pilgrim performing ʿumrah stop reciting the talbiyah according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling about where a person performing ʿumrah should stop reciting the talbiyah. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام identifies a known location in Makkah by local landmarks, showing the practical precision of rulings related to hajj and ʿumrah rites.
